{{Short description|Math concept}}
In [[functional analysis]], a set-valued mapping <math>A:X\to 2^X</math> where ''X'' is a real [[Hilbert space]] is said to be '''strongly monotone''' if
:<math>\exists c > 0 \mbox{ s.t. } \langle u - v , x - y \rangle \geq c \|x - y\|^2 \quad \forall x,y\in X, u\in Ax, v\in Ay</math>.
This is analogous to the notion of [[strictly increasing]] for scalar-valued functions of one scalar argument.

Equivalently, a [[binary relation]] <math>R \subseteq X^2</math> is strongly monotone if
:<math>\exists c > 0 \mbox{ s.t. } \langle u - v, x - y \rangle \geq c \| x - y \|^2 \quad \forall \langle x, u \rangle, \langle y, v \rangle \in R</math>.

A [[function (mathematics)|function]] <math>f : X \to X</math> is strongly monotone if
:<math>\exists c > 0 \mbox{ s.t. } \langle f(x) - f(y), x - y \rangle \geq c \| x - y \|^2 \quad \forall x, y \in X</math>.
